mainTopic: Which תנא agrees with רב and with the משנה about sprinkling the blood when part of an offering is impure, and when the קרבן פסח is brought in טומאה
overview: The גמרא first gives a second answer for whose view רב follows. רב ruled that a פסח whose meat became טמא should not have its blood sprinkled, but if it was sprinkled, it counts. The גמרא shows from a ברייתא that רבי יהושע holds exactly this, unless the owners themselves are טמא מת. Next, the גמרא shows that the משנה's line about other קדשים also follows רבי יהושע: a כזית of pure meat or a כזית of pure fat is enough to sprinkle the blood. The גמרא finds the source for this in the פסוק 'והקטיר החלב לריח ניחח', and explains why both 'חלב' and 'ריח ניחוח' are needed. Then a new משנה teaches that when most of the community, or the כהנים, are טמא, the פסח is brought in טומאה. If only a minority is טמא, that minority waits for פסח שני. רב חסדא and רבא argue about an impure knife, and the debate turns on whether טומאה is only pushed aside (דחויה) for the ציבור. The עמוד ends with רב and רב כהנא arguing whether an exact half counts as a majority, and a second version of רב כהנא's view that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A second answer: רב follows רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers an alternative source for רב's ruling: he holds like רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: רב, who said 'if he sprinkled it is accepted,' holds like רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, alternative answer to the question 'whose view does רב follow?' Here it says רב follows רבי יהושע. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ruled that a פסח whose meat became impure should not have its blood sprinkled, but if it was sprinkled, it still counts. The גמרא already linked this to one תנא. Now it says you could also link it to רבי יהושע, who holds that eating the meat is not essential for the offering to be accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces an alternative answer
The early אמורא whose ruling is being explained
It was accepted (the offering is valid, its owner is atoned/fulfilled)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
phrases.notes: Signals an alternative answer to the previous question

phrases.english: Rav, who said (if he sprinkled it is accepted), holds like Rabbi Yehoshua.
phrases.notes: Refers back to רב's ruling of 'ואם זרק הורצה'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, רַב דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the earlier question of which תנא רב follows (earlier)
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative attribution: assigning רב's view to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's ruling could only be grounded in the first תנא suggested earlier
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's ruling can also be grounded in רבי יהושע, who holds that eating is not essential

steps.title: רבי יהושע's general rule for all offerings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: for all offerings, if either the meat or the fat stays pure, the blood may be sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא, רבי יהושע says: with all offerings in the Torah, whether the meat became impure and the fat is still pure, or the fat became impure and the meat is still pure, one sprinkles the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what רבי יהושע holds. This first part is his general rule for ordinary offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood can be sprinkled as long as either part of the animal is still usable. The meat is for eating and the fat is for burning on the מזבח. For regular offerings, one pure part is enough. This rule sets the background. The next step shows the special cases where רבי יהושע is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
Animal offerings
Became ritually impure
The fats that are burned on the מזבח
Sprinkles/throws the blood on the מזבח, the key act that makes the offering count

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita, Rabbi Yehoshua says:
All the offerings in the Torah:
whether the meat became impure and the fat remains (pure),
or the fat became impure and the meat remains (pure),
one sprinkles the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for the claim that רב follows רבי יהושע
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע holds a view matching רב's ruling

steps.title: נזיר and פסח: don't sprinkle, but after the fact it counts
steps.stepSummary: For נזיר and פסח, if only the meat is impure, one should not sprinkle. But if he did, it is accepted. This matches רב exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a נזיר and one bringing a פסח: if the fat became impure and the meat is still pure, one sprinkles the blood. If the meat became impure and the fat is still pure, one does not sprinkle the blood. But if he sprinkled it, it is accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the proof. רבי יהושע says that for נזיר and פסח, impure meat means you should not sprinkle. But if you did, the offering counts, which is exactly רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For these two offerings, eating the meat is part of the מצוה itself. So when the meat is impure, we should not sprinkle from the start (לכתחילה). Still, 'ואם זרק הורצה' shows that eating is not essential after the fact (בדיעבד). That is precisely what רב said about the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow of נזירות and brings offerings at its end
One who brings the קרבן פסח
And if he (already) sprinkled: after-the-fact case

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the exact wording רב used: 'ואם זרק הורצה'. It shows that רבי יהושע separates what you should do from the start (don't sprinkle) from what counts after the fact (it is accepted).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. If the fat is impure and the meat pure, you sprinkle even from the start. Only when the meat is impure do we say 'don't sprinkle, but if you did it counts.' For these offerings, the meat matters more than the fat.

phrases.english: A nazirite and one who performs the Paschal offering:
if the fat became impure and the meat remains (pure),
one sprinkles the blood.
If the meat became impure and the fat remains (pure),
one does not sprinkle the blood,
phrases.notes: Because eating is part of the מצוה for these offerings

phrases.english: but if he sprinkled, it was accepted.
phrases.notes: Matches רב's ruling exactly

steps.triggerLanguage: נָזִיר וְעוֹשֵׂה פֶסַח, נִטְמָא חֵלֶב וּבָשָׂר קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the special cases that directly prove the claim
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that a פסח with impure meat is accepted if the blood was already sprinkled
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's words 'ואם זרק הורצה' in the ברייתא

steps.title: If the owners became impure from a corpse, it does not count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a limit: if the owners became טמא מת, the sprinkling does not work even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owners became impure from a corpse, one should not sprinkle. And if he did sprinkle, it was not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with one more case. When the owners themselves are impure from a dead body, sprinkling the blood does not count at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case, only the meat was impure; the owners were still fit to eat. Here the people themselves cannot eat, which is far worse. So even after the fact, the offering is not accepted. 'Eating is not essential' only applies when the owners are personally fit.

keyTerms.meaning: The owners of the offering
Impurity from contact with a dead body
It was not accepted

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע has three levels. (1) For ordinary offerings, either part pure is enough: sprinkle. The same holds for נזיר and פסח when the fat is impure and the meat is pure. (2) Impure meat for נזיר or פסח: don't sprinkle, but if done, it counts. This is רב's view. (3) Owners טמא מת: don't sprinkle, and if done, it does not count.

phrases.english: If the owners became impure from a corpse,
one should not sprinkle,
and if he sprinkled, it was not accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by adding a stricter case that sets the limit of רבי יהושע's leniency
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the owners are טמא מת, sprinkling the blood does not make the offering accepted, even after the fact

steps.title: Who wrote the משנה about other offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, 'with other offerings it is not so,' and asks which תנא it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'With other offerings it is not so,' etc. Who is the author of our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks whose opinion it follows. This sets up a new discussion; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that for other offerings, impure meat does not stop the sprinkling as long as the fat is pure. That treats eating as unimportant there, unlike פסח. The גמרא wants to identify which תנא holds this, since it seems to fit some views but not others.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated items; here, other offerings
It is not so: the rule is different
Who is the author of our משנה?

phrases.english: With (other) consecrated offerings it is not so, etc.
phrases.notes: Quotation from the משנה

phrases.english: Who is (the author of) our mishna?

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמּוּקְדָּשִׁין אֵינוֹ כֵּן וְכוּ׳. מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion of רב and opens a new topic about the next clause of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds that for other offerings, impure meat does not prevent sprinkling the blood

steps.title: The answer: it follows רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The line in the משנה follows רבי יהושע. In a ברייתא he rules that a כזית of meat or a כזית of fat is enough to sprinkle the blood. Half of each is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהושע. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהושע says, for every offering in the Torah, if an olive-size of meat or an olive-size of fat is left, the כהן sprinkles the blood. If only half an olive-size of meat and half an olive-size of fat are left, he does not sprinkle the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The משנה's line ('with other offerings it is not so') matches רבי יהושע, and the גמרא brings a ברייתא to show his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע, a כזית of fat alone is enough to sprinkle the blood, even if no pure meat is left. That is exactly what the משנה says about 'other offerings'. But half a כזית of meat plus half a כזית of fat do not add up to one כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
An olive-size, the minimum halachic amount
Meat (the part that is eaten)
Fat (the part burned on the altar)
He sprinkles the blood on the altar

steps.confusionAlert: Why don't half a כזית of meat and half a כזית of fat add up to one כזית? Because they have different jobs. The meat is eaten by people, and the fat is burned on the altar. So they do not combine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This identifies the תנא behind the משנה's ruling. It also shows that fat by itself can make the blood fit to be sprinkled.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehoshua.
As it was taught: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
All the offerings in the Torah
from which an olive-bulk of meat remained
or an olive-bulk of fat
one sprinkles the blood.

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בָּשָׂר וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת חֵלֶב
phrases.english: Half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of fat
one does not sprinkle the blood.
phrases.notes: Meat and fat do not combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5 by naming the תנא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהושע, who allows sprinkling when a כזית of fat alone remains.

steps.title: Special rules for an עולה and a מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. For an עולה, half of each does combine, since all of it is burned. For a מנחה, even if all of it stays pure, the blood is not sprinkled because of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: With an עולה, even if only half an olive-size of meat and half an olive-size of fat are left, the כהן sprinkles the blood, because all of it is burned on the altar. With a מנחה, even if all of it is still there, he does not sprinkle.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי יהושע continues with two special cases: the עולה and the מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an עולה, the meat and the fat are both burned on the altar. Since they have the same job, half and half do add up to a כזית. A pure מנחה, however, does not let the כהן sprinkle the blood of the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt-offering, entirely burned on the altar
Wholly consumed (burned completely)
Meal-offering (made of flour)
Remains (here: still whole and pure)

phrases.english: And with a burnt-offering, even half an olive-bulk of meat
and half an olive-bulk of fat
one sprinkles the blood,
because it is all wholly consumed.

phrases.aramaic: וּבַמִּנְחָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכּוּלָּהּ קַיֶּימֶת
phrases.english: And with a meal-offering, even though all of it remains
one may not sprinkle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with exceptions to its general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עולה's half-meat and half-fat combine, since all of it is burned. A pure מנחה does not allow sprinkling.

steps.title: Why is a מנחה mentioned here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a מנחה has to do with sprinkling blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the מנחה doing here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by the last line of the ברייתא. A מנחה is made of flour and has no blood, so why mention it? This question sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole ברייתא is about when the blood may be sprinkled. A flour offering seems to have nothing to do with that. So the גמרא needs to know which case the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: What is its business here? (What is it doing here?)

phrases.english: A meal-offering, what is it doing here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the relevance of the מנחה clause in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which מנחה is meant, and how does it connect to sprinkling blood?

steps.title: It is the מנחה brought with the libations
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that it is the מנחת נסכים that comes with an animal offering. The ברייתא teaches that even though it comes because of the animal, it does not count as the animal itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it means the מנחת נסכים. You might have thought that since it comes because of the animal offering, it is like the offering itself. So the ברייתא teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. The ברייתא means the flour offering that is brought together with an animal offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the animal became impure but its מנחת נסכים stayed pure. One might think the pure מנחה counts as 'part of the animal', and so the blood could be sprinkled. The ברייתא tells us that this is wrong: the מנחה does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The meal-offering brought with the libations of an animal offering
It might enter your mind to say
Because of (by the power of) the animal offering
It teaches us (that this is not so)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: the meal-offering of libations.
It might enter your mind to say,
since it comes because of the offering
it is like the offering itself.
So it teaches us that it is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the מנחת נסכים. Even though it comes because of the animal, it does not count as the animal for allowing the blood to be sprinkled.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the מנחת נסכים comes because of the animal, it should count like the animal itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: It does not count, so it cannot make the blood fit to be sprinkled.

steps.title: What is the source that fat alone is enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that fat alone allows the blood to be sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know the rule about the fat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source. How do we know that pure fat alone, with no pure meat, is enough to sprinkle the blood? This sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a כזית of fat is enough. But one might think the blood is mainly sprinkled so that the meat can be eaten. So the גמרא wants a פסוק showing that fat alone counts.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?

phrases.english: Fat, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main rule of the ברייתא (Step 6) and asks for its scriptural source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that fat alone allows the blood to be sprinkled.

steps.title: The פסוק: 'and he shall burn the fat'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי ישמעאל (some say רבי יהושע בן חנניה), brings the פסוק 'והקטיר החלב'. It shows that fat counts even without meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ישמעאל, and some trace it to רבי יהושע בן חנניה: the פסוק says, 'and he shall burn the fat as a pleasing smell to ה׳'. This means fat alone counts, even if there is no meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source: a פסוק that mentions burning the fat right after sprinkling the blood, without mentioning meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins the sprinkling of the blood to the burning of the fat. This shows that pure fat alone is a good enough reason to sprinkle the blood, even with no pure meat. This is the basis for רבי יהושע's view, and so for the משנה's line about 'other offerings'.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
And some trace it (attribute it) to
The verse
And he shall burn (on the altar)
As a pleasing smell

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהושע, the blood may be sprinkled if a כזית of pure meat or a כזית of pure fat remains. The source for fat alone is 'והקטיר החלב'. Meat and fat combine only in an עולה, and a pure מנחת נסכים does not count.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָטוּ בַּהּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה,
phrases.english: and some trace it to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya,
for the verse states:
"And he shall burn the fat as a pleasing smell to the Lord,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא יז:ו

phrases.aramaic: חֵלֶב — אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּשָׂר.
phrases.english: fat, even though there is no meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'והקטיר החלב לריח ניחח' shows that the blood may be sprinkled for the fat alone, even without meat.

steps.title: What is the source for the liver lobe and kidneys?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that fat has a source, and asks for a source for the יותרת הכבד and two kidneys.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for fat. For the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says we now have a source that fat alone allows the blood to be sprinkled. It asks: what about the other altar parts, the יותרת הכבד and the two kidneys?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'והקטיר החלב' only says 'fat'. The יותרת הכבד and kidneys are also burned on the מזבח, but they are not fat. So the earlier source does not obviously cover them.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source)
The lobe (appendage) of the liver, also translated as the diaphragm, which is burned on the altar
Kidneys
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: We have found [a source for] fat.
The lobe of the liver and the two kidneys,
phrases.notes: These are also altar parts (אימורים), but they are not fat.

phrases.english: from where do we know [that they are enough]?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן חֵלֶב. יוֹתֶרֶת הַכָּבֵד וּשְׁתֵּי כְלָיוֹת, מְנָא לַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the source search from fat (Step 11) to the other altar parts.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source showing that the יותרת הכבד and two kidneys alone allow זריקת הדם.

steps.title: Where did we say these parts allow sprinkling?
steps.stepSummary: Before looking for a source, the גמרא asks where we even learned that these parts allow the blood to be sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where did we say that we sprinkle [the blood because of them]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses and asks: who said the liver lobe and kidneys allow sprinkling at all? It is setting up the next step, which shows where this rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only need a source for a rule if the rule really exists. The ברייתא never said in so many words that these parts allow sprinkling. So the גמרא first makes sure the rule is real.

keyTerms.meaning: Where did we say?
We sprinkle (the blood on the altar)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on the question in Step 12. It is a short check that the rule really exists before the גמרא searches for its source.

phrases.english: Where did we say that we sprinkle [the blood in such a case]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the starting point of Step 12's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where it is taught that the יותרת הכבד and kidneys allow זריקת הדם.

steps.title: The rule comes from a דיוק in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a מנחה does not allow sprinkling. This implies that the liver lobe and kidneys do. So the question returns: what is the source?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it teaches: 'For a מנחה, even if all of it is still there, he should not sprinkle.' Only a מנחה does not allow it. But the liver lobe and two kidneys are fine. So where do we learn that from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 13. The rule comes from a דיוק (careful reading) of the ברייתא. Then it asks the source question of Step 12 again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא singled out the מנחה as something that does not allow sprinkling. That suggests the parts of the animal itself, like the liver lobe and kidneys, do allow it. Now that the rule is confirmed, the need for a פסוק is real.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it teaches
Remains (still there and pure)
It is fine, it is permitted

phrases.english: From the fact that it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: וּבַמִּנְחָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכּוּלָּהּ קַיֶּימֶת —
phrases.english: And with a meal-offering, even though all of it remains,
phrases.notes: The end of the ברייתא (Step 7), about the מנחת נסכים (Step 9).

phrases.english: he may not sprinkle [the blood].
It is a meal-offering that does not [allow sprinkling],
but the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys,
are fine [for sprinkling the blood].
From where do we know this?
phrases.notes: The source question of Step 12 returns.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָתָנֵי: וּבַמִּנְחָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכּוּלָּהּ קַיֶּימֶת — לֹא יִזְרוֹק.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 and then restates the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule comes from a דיוק in the ברייתא: only a מנחה is excluded, so the animal's altar parts do allow sprinkling.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'For a pleasing aroma' includes all burned parts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, speaking in his own name, learns from 'לריח ניחח' that anything burned as a pleasing aroma counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן himself said: the פסוק says 'for a pleasing aroma'. That means anything you burn up as a pleasing aroma.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the source for the liver lobe and kidneys. The same פסוק also says 'לריח ניחח', and that covers every part burned on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (Step 11) רבי יוחנן quoted a תנא. Here he speaks on his own (דידיה). The words 'לריח ניחח' are broad, so they include the liver lobe and kidneys, which are also burned for a pleasing aroma.

keyTerms.meaning: His own (in his own name, not quoting someone else)
For a pleasing (satisfying) aroma
You burn up (offer up on the altar)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan himself said,
phrases.notes: In his own name, unlike Step 11 where he quoted a תנא.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'For a pleasing aroma',
anything that you burn up for a pleasing aroma.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דִּידֵיהּ אָמַר, אָמַר קְרָא: ״לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source asked for in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לריח ניחח' includes every part burned on the מזבח, such as the liver lobe and kidneys.

steps.title: Why the Torah needed both 'fat' and 'pleasing aroma'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why both words are needed. 'חלב' alone would leave out the liver lobe and kidneys. 'ריח ניחוח' alone would include even a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to write 'fat', and it was necessary to write 'pleasing aroma'. If the תורה had written only 'fat', I would say: fat yes, but the liver lobe and two kidneys no. So the תורה wrote 'for a pleasing aroma'. And if the תורה had written only 'for a pleasing aroma', I would say: everything that goes up as a pleasing aroma counts, even a מנחה. So the תורה wrote 'fat'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that neither word is extra. Each word fixes a mistake we might make if we only had the other one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חלב' alone is too narrow, because it would leave out the liver lobe and kidneys. 'ריח ניחוח' alone is too broad, because it would let even a מנחה count. Together they cover exactly the altar parts of the animal itself.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
I would have thought (the mistaken first idea)
Yes

steps.whatToRemember: Only parts of the animal itself allow זריקת הדם: fat, the יותרת הכבד and the kidneys. A מנחה does not, even if it comes with the animal. 'חלב' keeps the rule limited to the animal, and 'ריח ניחוח' widens it to all of the animal's altar parts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic צריכותא. It shows how the גמרא proves that each word in a פסוק teaches something of its own.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write 'fat'
and it was necessary to write 'pleasing aroma',
because if the Merciful One had written [only] 'fat',
I would have said: fat, yes,
the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys, no.
So the Merciful One wrote: 'for a pleasing aroma'.
And if the Merciful One had written [only] 'for a pleasing aroma',

phrases.aramaic: הָוֵה אָמֵינָא: כׇּל הָעוֹלִין לְרֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ,
phrases.english: I would have said: everything that goes up for a pleasing aroma [counts],
even a meal-offering.
So the Merciful One wrote 'fat'.
phrases.notes: 'Fat' limits the rule to parts of the animal itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב חֵלֶב וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב ״רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why both sources (Steps 11 and 15) are needed and do not repeat each other.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both words are needed. 'ריח ניחוח' includes all of the animal's altar parts, and 'חלב' leaves out the מנחה.

steps.title: New משנה: When the פסח is brought in impurity
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the whole community or most of it is impure, or the כהנים are impure, the קרבן פסח is brought in טומאה. If only a minority is impure, the pure bring it on the first פסח and the impure bring it on פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the whole community or most of it became impure, or if the כהנים were impure and the community was pure, they bring the פסח in impurity. If a minority of the community became impure, the pure ones bring the first פסח and the impure ones bring the second פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the rule for when the קרבן פסח is brought even though people are impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key factor is how many people are impure. If most or all are impure, or if the כהנים who do the service are impure, the rule of impurity is pushed aside and they go ahead in טומאה. If only a minority is impure, nothing is pushed aside, and those impure people must wait for פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The community, the Jewish people as a whole
Most of it, a majority
A minority
In a state of ritual impurity
The second פסח, a month later, for those who missed the first

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a large number of impure people is enough. What matters is majority versus minority. Even many thousands of impure people still go to פסח שני if they are less than half.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: If the community or most of it became impure,
or if the priests were impure
and the community was pure —
they should perform it in impurity.
If a minority of the community became impure —
the pure ones perform the first Pesach,
phrases.notes: On the 14th of ניסן

phrases.english: and the impure ones perform the second.
phrases.notes: On the 14th of אייר, פסח שני

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה and a new topic, separate from the earlier discussion of what allows the blood to be sprinkled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A majority of impure people, or impure כהנים, means the פסח is brought in טומאה. An impure minority waits for פסח שני.

steps.title: ברייתא: Impure vessels also allow bringing the offering in impurity
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three cases: impure ישראל with pure כהנים and כלים, pure ישראל with impure כהנים and כלים, and even pure ישראל and כהנים with only impure כלי שרת. In all three, they bring the קרבן in טומאה, because a קרבן ציבור is not divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If ישראל were impure and the כהנים and כלי שרת were pure, or ישראל were pure and the כהנים and כלי שרת were impure, and even if ישראל and the כהנים were pure and only the כלי שרת were impure, they bring it in impurity. This is because a קרבן ציבור is not split up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that expands the משנה. It adds a new case, impure Temple vessels, to the list of situations that allow bringing the קרבן in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is the third case. Even when every person is pure, impure כלי שרת are enough to let the whole service go ahead in טומאה. The reason is that a קרבן ציבור is not divided: once part of the service must be done in טומאה, all of it may be done that way.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Sacred vessels used in the בית המקדש service
A communal offering
Divided, split into parts

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a קרבן ציבור is not divided explains why one impure element is enough to let the entire service be done in טומאה.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
If the Jewish people were impure
and the priests and sacred vessels were pure,
or the Jewish people were pure
and the priests and sacred vessels were impure,
and even if the Jewish people and priests were pure
and only the sacred vessels were impure —
they should perform it in impurity,
because a communal offering is not divided.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל טְמֵאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה by adding impure כלי שרת as another case of going ahead in טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure כלי שרת, even when all the people are pure, allow the קרבן to be brought in טומאה, because a קרבן ציבור is not divided.

steps.title: רב חסדא limits the vessel case to a knife impure from a corpse
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the ברייתא's case of impure כלי שרת applies only when the knife became impure from a טמא מת. He bases this on the פסוק 'בחלל חרב', from which we learn that a metal sword is treated like the corpse itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: They only taught this when the knife became impure from someone impure from a dead body. The Torah says 'בחלל חרב', which teaches that a sword is like the corpse.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא narrows the ברייתא. He explains that not every impure vessel counts, only a knife with a very severe level of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From 'בחלל חרב' we learn that metal touching a source of מת impurity takes on that same severe level. So a knife that touched a טמא מת becomes an אב הטומאה, as impure as the person it touched. A knife with weaker impurity is not included in the ברייתא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of (introduces a limitation)
Knife, here the slaughtering knife
A person impure from contact with a dead body
A sword is like the corpse, so metal gets the same impurity level as what it touched

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
They only taught this
when the knife became impure from one impure from a corpse,
for the Merciful One said: "one slain by a sword,"
phrases.notes: במדבר יט:טז

phrases.english: a sword is like the corpse,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא's third case, impure כלי שרת, to one specific kind of impurity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure כלי שרת allow bringing the קרבן in טומאה only when the knife got severe impurity from a טמא מת, based on 'חרב הרי הוא כחלל'.

steps.title: Why the knife matters: it makes the person impure
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא finishes his reason. A knife at this severe level makes the שוחט impure. So from the very start, the service is being done with טומאת הגוף, the kind of bodily impurity that normally carries כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The knife makes the person impure. So from the start, when the service is done, it is done with bodily impurity of the כרת kind.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains why only this kind of impure knife counts. It turns the case into one where a person, not just a tool, is impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the knife is an אב הטומאה, the person using it becomes impure. That brings the case back to טומאת הגוף, the same kind of impurity the משנה already allows to be pushed aside for the ציבור. A weaker impure knife would not make the person impure, so it would not fit this reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes the person impure
From the start, from the beginning
Impurity of the body, of the person himself
Spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for an impure person who eats קדשים

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא says impure כלי שרת allow the קרבן to be brought in טומאה. רב חסדא limits this to a knife impure from a טמא מת, because only that knife makes the person impure, which turns the case into טומאת הגוף.

phrases.english: and it makes the person impure,
so that from the start, when it is performed —
with bodily impurity of the karet kind
it is being performed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב חסדא's reason by explaining why the knife's severe impurity matters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A knife that touched a טמא מת makes the שוחט impure, so the service is done from the start in טומאת הגוף. That is why this case of impure כלי שרת allows going ahead in טומאה.

steps.title: A knife made impure by a שרץ: only pure people may take part
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא contrasts his case with a knife made impure by a שרץ. Such a knife makes only the meat impure, not the person. So pure people may do the service, but impure people may not. Eating impure meat is only a לאו, while eating with טומאת הגוף carries כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the knife became impure from a שרץ, it only makes the meat impure, not the person. Then pure people may do the service, and impure people may not. Better that the meat be eaten while the meat is impure, which is only a regular prohibition, than that it be eaten by someone whose body is impure, which carries כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא finishes his statement by giving the opposite case, a knife made impure by a שרץ, to show why his rule is limited to טמא מת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A knife that touched a שרץ is only one level removed from the source of impurity. At that level it can make food impure, but it cannot make a person impure. So the שוחט stays pure. In that case we have a choice, and we pick the lighter problem: impure meat (a לאו) instead of impure people (כרת).

keyTerms.meaning: A creeping creature; a source of impurity weaker than a dead body
To the man, meaning to the person
Impurity of the meat itself
It is better
A regular negative commandment, which carries lashes and not כרת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of impurity. 'טומאת בשר' means the MEAT is impure. 'טומאת הגוף' means the PERSON eating is impure. The second one is the more severe.

phrases.english: But if the knife became impure with the impurity of a creeping creature,
it is the meat that it makes impure,
but it does not make the person impure.
phrases.notes: A secondary source of impurity can affect food but not people.

phrases.english: Pure people perform the service; impure people do not perform it,
for it is better that it be eaten with impurity of the meat, which is only a negative commandment,
and that the meat not be eaten with bodily impurity,
which carries the penalty of karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the contrasting half of רב חסדא's limitation from steps 19–20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the knife is impure from a שרץ, only pure people may bring and eat the פסח. This keeps the impurity at the lighter level of a לאו and away from כרת.

steps.title: The גמרא infers that רב חסדא holds impurity is only pushed aside for the community
steps.stepSummary: From רב חסדא's effort to keep impurity to a minimum, the גמרא concludes that he holds טומאה דחויה בציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that רב חסדא holds that impurity is pushed aside for the community, not fully permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and names the general principle behind רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If impurity were fully permitted (הותרה) for the community, there would be no reason to prefer pure people. Because רב חסדא still prefers them whenever possible, impurity must only be pushed aside (דחויה) under pressure. That means we allow as little impurity as we can.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently; we see from here
He holds
Impurity is only 'pushed aside'. It is allowed only as far as it is needed, not fully permitted
The community

steps.whyThisMatters: The question of דחויה versus הותרה is a major issue across the סוגיות of קרבנות ציבור that are brought in impurity.

phrases.english: Apparently, Rav Chisda holds:
Impurity is overridden (only pushed aside) in the case of the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This draws the underlying principle out of רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חסדא holds טומאה דחויה בציבור, so even in a community setting we keep impurity as small as possible.

steps.title: רבי יצחק states the same principle outright
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says openly what the גמרא just inferred from רב חסדא: טומאה דחויה בציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too רבי יצחק said: impurity is pushed aside for the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from another אמורא who says the same principle in plain words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רב חסדא the principle was only an inference. רבי יצחק says it directly. This shows the view is an established position and not just a reading of רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too said; introduces a supporting statement

phrases.english: And so too Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Impurity is overridden in the case of the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This supports the inference made in step 22.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The explicit statement of רבי יצחק

steps.title: רבא disagrees: even impure people may take part
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that even impure people may bring the פסח when the impurity comes from the knife. He brings a פסוק as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: even impure people may also do it. Why? Because it is written: 'And the meat that touches anything impure shall not be eaten; it shall be burned in fire. And as for the meat, anyone pure may eat meat.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens an opposing view. He allows even impure people to bring and eat the פסח when the knife was made impure by a שרץ, and he quotes a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא limited the service to pure people. רבא says there is no need for that. He does not yet explain how the פסוק proves it; that comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
They perform (the service)
What is the reason?
It shall be burned

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Even impure people may also perform it.
What is the reason? As it is written:
'And the meat that touches anything impure'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ז:יט

phrases.english: 'shall not be eaten; it shall be burned in fire;'
'and as for the meat, anyone who is pure may eat meat.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ טְמֵאִין נָמֵי עָבְדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא argues with רב חסדא's ruling in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the knife is impure from a שרץ, even impure people may bring and eat the פסח.

steps.title: רבא's reading: the two halves of the פסוק go together
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the requirement 'anyone pure may eat' applies only where impure meat is forbidden. Where impure meat is allowed, impure people are allowed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wherever we do not apply 'the meat that touches anything impure shall not be eaten,' we also do not apply 'anyone pure may eat meat.' Wherever we do apply 'the meat that touches anything impure shall not be eaten,' we also apply 'anyone pure may eat meat.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains how the פסוק proves his ruling. The two halves of the פסוק are linked: they both apply together, or neither applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the meat is impure, yet it may still be eaten. So the first half ('impure meat shall not be eaten') is not in force. Since the second half ('only the pure may eat') is tied to the first, it falls away as well. That means impure people may eat too.

keyTerms.meaning: Wherever; in any case where
We apply (literally 'read') this verse to it

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא holds טומאה דחויה בציבור, so we keep impurity minimal: only pure people may take part. רבא links the two halves of the פסוק: if the impure meat is allowed, impure people are allowed too.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying that the rule 'only the pure may eat' is ever cancelled on its own. It falls away only in a case where the first half of the פסוק (impure meat is forbidden) has already fallen away.

phrases.english: Wherever we do not apply to it

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהַבָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בְּכׇל טָמֵא לֹא יֵאָכֵל״,
phrases.english: 'the meat that touches anything impure shall not be eaten,'
we do not apply to it
'and as for the meat, anyone pure may eat meat.'
Wherever we do apply to it

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהַבָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בְּכׇל טָמֵא לֹא יֵאָכֵל״,
phrases.english: 'the meat that touches anything impure shall not be eaten,'
we apply to it
'and as for the meat, anyone pure may eat meat.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This explains how the פסוק cited in step 24 supports רבא's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two halves of the פסוק stand or fall together. Where impure meat may be eaten, impure people may eat it too.

steps.title: Dispute: Does exactly half count as a majority?
steps.stepSummary: רב and רב כהנא argue about a case where exactly half of the people are טהורין and half are טמאין. רב says half is like a majority, and רב כהנא says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if the Jewish people were half pure and half impure, רב said half-and-half is like a majority. רב כהנא said half-and-half is not like a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a new argument between two אמוראים about a 50/50 split of pure and impure people at פסח time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that when most of the public is טמא, they bring the פסח in טומאה. This case is right on the edge, because neither side is a majority. רב treats half as strong enough to count like a majority, and רב כהנא does not. The practical meaning of each view comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated: introduces an argument between אמוראים
Exactly half and half: an even split
Like a majority: has the legal status of most of the group
People who are ritually pure
People who are ritually impure

phrases.english: It was stated:
phrases.notes: Signals a new dispute between אמוראים.

phrases.english: If the Jewish people were
half pure and half impure,

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה כְּרוֹב.
phrases.english: Rav said: half-and-half is like a majority.
And Rav Kahana said:
half-and-half is not like a majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר. הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֶחֱצָה טְהוֹרִין וּמֶחֱצָה טְמֵאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the knife-impurity discussion and opens a new case: an even split between pure and impure people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a 50/50 split counts like a majority. רב כהנא: it does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the boundary of the משנה's 'majority impure' rule. We learn whether exactly half is enough to allow the פסח to be brought in טומאה.

steps.title: רב's view in practice: each half brings its own פסח
steps.stepSummary: According to רב, since each half counts like a majority, the pure group brings the פסח in purity and the impure group brings it in impurity, both on the first פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said half-and-half is like a majority. This means these people bring for themselves, and those people bring for themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב's view actually means for what people do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half is treated like a majority. So the impure half gets the same rights as a 'majority impure' public: they bring the פסח in טומאה and are not pushed off to פסח שני. The pure half brings its פסח normally, in purity.

keyTerms.meaning: These ones: here, each of the two groups
They bring for themselves: each group brings its own פסח

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה כְּרוֹב:
phrases.english: Rav said half-and-half is like a majority:
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats רב's words in order to explain them.

phrases.english: these (the pure) bring for themselves,
and those (the impure) bring for themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה כְּרוֹב: הַלָּלוּ עוֹשִׂין לְעַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical result of רב's opinion from step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both halves bring the פסח on the first פסח: the pure in purity and the impure in טומאה.

steps.title: רב כהנא's view in practice: the impure wait for פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: According to רב כהנא, half is not a majority. So the pure bring the first פסח, and the impure bring פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said half-and-half is not like a majority. So the pure bring the first פסח, and the impure bring the second פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב כהנא's view means for what people do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the impure half is not a majority, it does not get the special permission to bring the פסח in טומאה. Instead, they are treated like individual impure people, who make it up on פסח שני a month later.

keyTerms.meaning: The first פסח, brought on 14 ניסן
The second פסח, brought on 14 אייר by those who could not bring the first
Is not like a majority: does not get majority status

phrases.english: And Rav Kahana said
half-and-half is not like a majority:
the pure bring the first (Pesach),
and the impure bring the second (Pesach).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה אֵינוֹ כְּרוֹב: טְהוֹרִין עוֹשִׂין אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical result of רב כהנא's side, as the parallel to רב's explanation in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pure people bring פסח ראשון, and impure people bring פסח שני.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: each half brings on the first פסח (the impure in טומאה). רב כהנא (first version): the pure bring on the first פסח, and the impure on פסח שני.

steps.title: A second version of רב כהנא's view begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another version (איכא דאמרי) of רב כהנא's view. It begins the same way: half is not a majority, and the pure bring the first פסח. The rest continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב כהנא said half-and-half is not like a majority, so the pure bring the first פסח...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a different report of what רב כהנא held. This line is a setup, and the new part of the ruling comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening matches the first version: half is not a majority, and the pure bring the first פסח. The difference will be about what happens to the impure half. That part comes at the start of the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces a different version of a statement
The אמורא whose view is being reported again
They bring the first פסח

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion argued against רב כהנא. It is a different report of what רב כהנא himself said. The two versions agree so far; the difference comes next.

phrases.english: Some say:
phrases.notes: Introduces an alternate version of the statement.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
half-and-half is not like a majority —
the pure bring the first (Pesach),
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of רב כהנא's view in place of the one explained in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version too, half is not a majority and the pure bring the first פסח. What happens to the impure half follows on the next עמוד.
